author: Parsifal-2045
body:
#### PR description:
This PR introduces a single host-side prefix-scan interface: `cms::alpakatools::prefixScan`, as planned in #50876, and migrates all CMSSW call sites to it.
The interface computes an inclusive prefix sum with input/output aliasing allowed, and dispatches automatically between the single-kernel `multiBlockPrefixScan` and the multi-kernel `iterativePrefixScan` depending on the problem size.

##### Dispatch rule

 - CPU single-thread-per-block backends (serial, TBB): serial scan via a new `serialPrefixScan` helper, shared with `iterativePrefixScan`; it waits on the queue first, so it stays correct on non-blocking CPU queues (even if I don't think they are currently used, the wait should be a no-op when using blocking queues anyway).
 - GPU backends: `multiBlockPrefixScan` when 2   size/1024   256 blocks, `iterativePrefixScan` otherwise (1-block problems and larger ones). At 256 blocks, `multiBlockPrefixScan` needs  (256+64) 8 B = 2.5 KB of shared memory, comfortably below the standard 48 KiB shared memory limit per block. The dispatch choice is exposed as a constant expression (`prefixScanUseMultiBlock`) and the boundaries are pinned in the added unit test via `static_assert`.

 ##### Working-point measurements (NVIDIA H100 NVL, `uint32`, 1024 threads/block)

 Saturated single queue, back-to-back launches:

Blocks | multiBlock (s) | iterative (s)
|:-------------:|:-----------------:|:----------------------:|
1 | 7.7 | 4.2
2 | 7.8 | 9.8
8 | 9.1 | 10
16 | 11.3 | 10.0
64 | 22.3 | 10.7
256 | ~65 | ~11
5860 (6M elements) | 1713.8 | 115.8

Busy GPU (more production-like) with 24 concurrent streams 

Blocks | multiBlock (s) | iterative (s)
|:-------------:|:-----------------:|:----------------------:|
2-96 | ~5 | ~12
192 | 7.7| 12.3
256 | 11.0 | 12.3
384 | 14.6 | 12.3
1024| 32.2 | 20.4
5860 (6M elements) | 182.0 | 104.3

Under contention, `iterativePrefixScan` pays the stream latency on each of its kernel launches (3-5 depending on the number of levels), while `multiBlockPrefixScan` has a single kernel launch regardless of the problem size.
I've set the switch conservatively at 256 blocks, and iterativePrefixScan takes over above ~500 blocks.
Testing on the PixelTracks chain with ~0.5M hits and ~6M doublets, the related scans improve by between 5 and 7 times.
At 1 block, the iterative implementation collapses to a single kernel without counter memset/atomics and wins ~2 over the multiBlock.

All 9 existing `multiBlockPrefixScan` call sites now use the unified interface (work division, block-counter buffer+memset, shared-memory check and warp-size lookup all internalised).
This unification also retires `checkSharedMemoryPrefixScan` and its exception, since the multiBlock implementation is only used for smaller problems.

I've added a new unified-interface section to the existing prefix scan unit test, verifying result correctness and making sure that the dispatch logic is sound.


#### PR validation:

Code compiles and unit tests complete without issues. Since the change is purely technical, I'll let the bot verify physics and timing/memory usage.
title: Introduce unified `cms::alpakatools::prefixScan` with automatic dispatch and migrate all `multiBlockPrefixScan` call sites
